title: Kenyan Chips Mayai
community: A Nairobi and urban Kenya institution
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Chips Mayai — Kenya's most beloved street food omelette. Freshly fried chips embedded in a spiced egg omelette, cooked until golden and set. The combination of crispy chips and soft, fragrant egg is completely irresistible and unmistakably Kenyan.
longDesc: Chips mayai (literally 'chips eggs' in Swahili) is one of the great Kenyan street food inventions — simple, cheap, filling, and somehow better than the sum of its parts. Freshly fried chips are tossed into a beaten egg omelette seasoned with onions, tomatoes, and coriander, then cooked in a pan until the egg sets around the chips like a frittata. Every Kenyan who has eaten it in the street at 9pm remembers it.
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes — peeled and cut into chips
equipment: Large flat pan or non-stick frying pan (for omelette)
steps: Fry the chips at 175°C until golden and crispy. Drain and season lightly with salt.
Beat the eggs with salt, pepper, and curry powder.
Add the diced onion, tomato, chilli, and coriander to the beaten egg. Stir to combine.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large flat pan over medium heat.
Add the fried chips to the pan in a single layer.
Pour the egg mixture over the chips, ensuring all chips are coated.
Cook without stirring for 3—4 minutes until the bottom is set and golden.
Flip carefully (using a plate to help) and cook the other side for 2—3 minutes.
Slide onto a cutting board. Cut into wedges. Serve with kachumbari.
chefTips: The chips must be freshly fried and hot when the egg goes on — cold chips produce a soggy result.
Use a plate larger than the pan to flip: place the plate on top, invert the pan, then slide the omelette back in.
The omelette should be golden and set on the outside but still slightly moist inside.
commonMistakes: Cold chips — the omelette does not set around them properly.
Too much egg — the chips drown in egg and the ratio is wrong.
Too high heat — burns the outside before the inside sets.

faqs.q: Is chips mayai the same as a frittata?
faqs.a: They are very similar in technique — both are egg dishes set around a filling in a pan. Chips mayai is the Kenyan version, using spiced egg with chips embedded in it. The flavour profile is distinctly Kenyan.

cookingScience: The chips embedded in the egg create pockets of steam during cooking as the moisture in the potato evaporates. This steam helps cook the egg from within, explaining why chips mayai sets more evenly than a flat omelette despite its thickness.
sustainabilityTips: Chips mayai is one of the most complete, filling meals achievable with minimal ingredients — excellent food efficiency.
reheating: Warm briefly in a pan — do not microwave.
culturalNote: Chips mayai is one of Nairobi's most celebrated street foods — the kind of meal that Kenyans living abroad specifically miss and return to immediately when they come home. It is cheap, filling, and packed with the flavours of home.
